description: Develop an analysis workflow to reconcile two synthetic reports of a batch transfer exercise. A reviewer must determine which discrepancies can be resolved from bounded records and which require a targeted follow-up request.
valued_outcome: For each of twelve batch identifiers, produce a reconciled quantity or explicit bounded disagreement, cite supporting records, and issue at most three follow-up requests that each name a missing field or record.
hard_constraints: Never silently drop duplicate or unmatched rows.
Use only the supplied unit-conversion table.
Do not infer missing quantities from neighboring batches.
Complete the review within sixty minutes.
resources: Two synthetic reports with thirty rows each, twelve batch identifiers, quantities, units and status fields.
Eight amendment records with explicit superseded-row references.
A table specifying that one fictional unit U equals five fictional units V, plus a status dictionary and report cutoff times.
Spreadsheet or local script environment and sixty minutes of reviewer time.
observations: Seven batches agree after applying the supplied conversion.
Three identifiers each occur twice in one report.

Awkward observation: the newer report includes an amendment whose effective time precedes both cutoffs, while the older report already includes its replacement quantity under a different row identifier.

known_parent_functions.function: A conversion table expresses quantities in a common unit.
known_parent_functions.operating_path: Apply the supplied factor to a recorded quantity and retain its original unit.
known_parent_functions.ordinary_use: Comparing quantities reported in different units.

known_parent_functions.function: A revision register preserves replacement relationships.
known_parent_functions.operating_path: Link an amendment to the specific earlier record it supersedes.

adverse_disturbance: Remove one superseded-row reference from an amendment and replace one status value with an undefined code before the final pass.
probe_resources: Two copies of the records, one with the disturbance and one without, and a sealed per-batch reconciliation key opened after outputs are frozen.
Twenty extra minutes to compare two workflow variants using resolved-batch counts, unsupported definite claims and follow-up-request counts.
